target_customer: Universities, counseling and social work programs, teletherapy companies, training organizations
problem: Counselors and clinicians have few ways to practice patient conversations at scale before real sessions.
business_model: B2B/B2edu per-institution licence (can be passed to students as a lab fee); a directory lists $49 a month for individuals (unverified)
product_category: AI patient simulation for healthcare training

founders.name: Vrishank Saini
previous_startups: Healthcare education app with 120,000+ downloads in six months (YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Met co-founder at the University of Chicago; Pulse2 (2025-03) says both reportedly dropped out. He failed a clinical communications exam and could not afford a $9,000 tutor, which started the product.

founders.name: Tiko Bdoyan
founders.background_notes: Lead ML researcher in a bioinformatics lab at the Luddy School of Informatics (YC launch post). YC profile says Tiko; the launch post and Pulse2 say Tigran; sources do not settle whether this is one person.

technical_complexity.rationale: Conversational avatars with LLM-driven patients and skill feedback, built by a two-person team in 2024; standard engineering with some hard parts. No source shows deep technical difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Curriculum and LMS integrations help; avatar and LLM approach is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the wedge. Other AI patient simulation startups (SimConverse, Xuron, EmpatiQ, VRpatients) appear in 2025-26 searches, with unverified dates.

market_need_then: YC launch post cites a doctor shortage and government mandates to expand medical school seats, which schools struggle to staff with actor-based patient simulations. Early tool reached 2,500 users and $5k MRR in three weeks (YC launch post, company-reported).

identity.mascot_or_character: Talking AI patient avatars in the product

rebrands.why: Not sourced; YC launch pages show both names and say 'previously Soma Lab'. The new name says what the product does (simulated care).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says what it does and is easy to spell, but generic; press is mostly funding announcements and university news, with no coverage of the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: SimCare (formerly Soma Lab), YC S24, grew from an AI communications coach into AI patient avatars for medical, counseling and nursing training. After being rejected once for S24 and reapplying, it raised a $2M seed in February 2025 co-led by YC and Drive Capital and reported 30 pilots, with University of Pennsylvania as a pilot customer and Touro and The Chicago School using it (2026 coverage). No later round, exit or shutdown found; the outcome is early and unresolved, with several AI patient-simulation startups entering the same space.
notes: Seed: $2M reported by HIT Consultant (2025-02-27), Pulse2 (2025-03-09) and HLTH (2025-02-28); lead investors YC and Drive Capital. YC's $500k standard deal is not recorded as a round. Competition: no source dated near the S24 batch found (SimConverse seed date could not be verified because the page opened was wrong); list left empty. Co-founder first name is Tiko on the YC profile and Tigran elsewhere. Pulse2's 'reportedly rejected then reapplied' and dropout claims are single-outlet. Pricing of $49 a month is from a directory. Name origin not found.
